name: HYDRA-UMC-DEV-SERVER
technologies: SQLite (durable task/state journal, from DS05 onward)
build: Ten-delivery plan (DS01-DS10, see this repository's own README Roadmap section): a reproducible development host (target platform: Raspberry Pi 5 or Compute Module 5, both 8GB, NVMe-booted) that hosts this ecosystem's source code, an isolated task/workspace runner for bounded programming/build/test work, and a durable queue coordinating with HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT's own incident lifecycle - never a new AI to train, never a replacement operating system, never itself the authority that decides a machine is safe. Real build: python -m build (see pyproject.toml).
deployment_target_note: "dev-server" is a new deployment_target value, not yet used elsewhere in this ecosystem's manifests (existing values: cm5, mobile, user-pc, wearable). It denotes a Raspberry Pi 5 / CM5 host dedicated to development and task execution - explicitly NOT the same physical role as "cm5" (the operational node that talks to real machines/robots). Documented here so HYDRA-UMC-UPDATER/the dashboard do not misread it as an operational CM5.
notes: Scaffolding v0.1.0 - DS01-DS10 of the 10-delivery plan, now complete (contracts, limits and a verifiable skeleton). DS01-DS03 only read and describe. DS01: state-ownership table + 17-relationship grouping + a real, tested configuration schema (config.py) whose default policy grants NO task deployment permission. DS02: validated remote-station profile + read-only host preflight + dry-run provisioning plan, never executed. DS03: conservative migration (migration.py) - hashes/classifies every file in a source checkout, records unpushed commits, plans each class into one of four provably-separate destinations, refuses a private file to a shareable root; the source is never touched. DS04: the first thing that executes - workspace.py refuses a path that escapes a per-task workspace (.., absolute, symlink-out) and refuses two tasks sharing one; recipe.py pins a revision and refuses any command not in the policy's own allowed_commands; runner.py runs that one allow-listed command in the isolated workspace with a SCRUBBED environment (no inherited *_TOKEN/*_KEY/*_SECRET/ANTHROPIC_*/GITHUB_*/SSH_*), under a bounded timeout, killing the whole process group on timeout or cancel - proven by a real test that spawns a child-of-a-child and confirms both die. It still deploys nothing. Injectable WorkspaceFs/ProcessLauncher seams keep the control tests off a real host. DS05: a durable SQLite queue (durable_queue.py) with leases and an append-only execution journal that survive a restart - a duplicate enqueue never becomes a second job, a crashed worker's lease expires and reconcile() returns the task to queued, a result from a worker that no longer holds the lease is rejected (never a false success), a base that moved since enqueue blocks promotion even on exit 0, and the journal keeps only bounded tails. DS06: an interchangeable AI provider behind a safety contract (ai_provider.py) - only the DETERMINISTIC FAKE ships (kind must be "fake"; a real provider and its authorization are a user decision). run_provider_step() turns a provider timeout / quota exhaustion / malformed output into a bounded named outcome (never an escalating exception), stops before a configured calls/tokens/cost budget would be exceeded, and treats the provider's answer as DATA never instructions - an "ignore previous instructions / deploy now / grant me root" suggestion is copied verbatim, flagged, and still grants_no_permissions / triggers_no_deploy for every outcome; the result is inert (wired to nothing). DS07: an authenticated incident transport (incident_transport.py) for the round trip with HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT - every message is HMAC-signed by a registered node with a nonce, timestamp and contract version; verify_message() rejects an unregistered identity, a bad signature, a node impersonating another, a replayed nonce, a stale timestamp, an overloaded sender and an incompatible version, each with a named code. IncidentSession runs the full submit -> diagnosis -> post-deploy-verification round trip (not just the submit); a dropped connection leaves it pending-ack and reconcile() re-sends the same incident with a fresh nonce, the peer de-duping on the stable incident_id so nothing is lost or double-counted. It is a real protocol object, never a manual file drop. DS08: one fully controlled repair cycle (repair_cycle.py) chaining repro-confirmed -> incident-raised -> candidate-received -> regression-passed -> build-test-passed -> approved -> installed -> verified (or -> recovered / -> blocked). Every step is gated: an unreproduced failure never opens the cycle; a candidate whose HMAC signature does not verify, or that is pinned to a different incident / base fingerprint / target, is blocked; regression and build-test must be genuinely green; an approval must be signed by a registered approver AND issued for this exact base and target; install goes through an injectable isolated-installer seam (never the real target); a failed post-install verification rolls back and ends the cycle recovered, and the I60/T07 apparent-success control voids the result (with rollback) if the base moved mid-cycle or the evidence is for a different repro case. DS09: stable operation + verified restore (operations.py) - create_backup() records a sha256 per file with a backup_id, instance_id and schema_version; verify_backup() re-hashes and flags drift; restore_backup() refuses a backup for a different instance id or schema version, or one whose files no longer match, otherwise restores the exact bytes. check_operational_health() reports a named finding for orphaned (expired-but-leased) entries, a journal over its row cap, and free disk under the floor. All filesystem contact is behind the injectable BackupFs seam. DS10: the delivery package + an HONEST maturity evaluation (delivery.py). build_delivery_manifest() enumerates what the repo actually ships (every module/doc/config plus pyproject/manifest/CHANGELOG/README) with a sha256 per file, and reads back the real CLI surface, version and test count. evaluate_maturity() reports each of the ten deliveries as shipped/partial/not-started against real evidence (DS06 is partial on purpose - only the deterministic fake ships), lists seven known limitations in plain words, and hard-codes overall_maturity to "scaffolding" - the code has no branch that returns anything higher, so the evaluation cannot over-claim. CLI: config / inventory / station / migrate / task / queue / provider / incident / repair / ops / deliver subcommands. The ten-delivery plan is complete; the maturity stays "scaffolding" by design - nothing here provisions a host, runs a deploy, or has touched target hardware, and `deliver evaluate` says exactly that.
